industry: Aerospace / Electric Vertical Takeoff and Landing (eVTOL)
thesis: Archer Aviation is a pre-revenue eVTOL developer racing to commercialize its four-passenger Midnight air taxi. The bull case rests on a fortress balance sheet — roughly $1.8B in Q1 2026 liquidity against under $100M of debt — that funds FAA type certification, an initial US launch under the eVTOL Integration Pilot Program, a UAE/Abu Dhabi program, official LA28 Olympics air-taxi status, and an expanding defense franchise anchored by the Anduril partnership. The counterweight is stark: FY2025 net loss of $618.2M, an adjusted EBITDA loss of $481.8M, no meaningful commercial revenue yet, and binary certification and dilution risk. With shares near $4.82 versus a ~$10.5 analyst average target, ACHR is a high-conviction, high-uncertainty speculative buy for risk-tolerant investors.

drivers: FAA type certification of Midnight achieved and initial US commercial operations launch on schedule
UAE/Abu Dhabi program and official LA28 Olympics air-taxi status convert into visible, revenue-generating routes
Anduril defense partnership scales into material hybrid-aircraft and program-of-record contracts
$1.8B liquidity carries the company to commercialization without a heavily dilutive raise, driving a re-rating toward analyst targets

base_case.assumptions: Certification progresses with typical eVTOL slippage; initial operations begin at limited scale in 2026-2027; defense and software initiatives add optionality; cash burn stays within guidance and liquidity funds the ramp; the stock re-rates toward the lower end of the ~$10.5 analyst average as milestones de-risk the story

risks: FAA certification slips materially, pushing commercial revenue years out
Adjusted EBITDA losses of $170M-$200M per quarter force dilutive capital raises that erode the share count
eVTOL sector sentiment sours or a competitor (Joby) reaches commercial operations first
Execution missteps in manufacturing scale-up or the UAE/US pilot programs undermine the commercialization narrative

catalysts.event: Q2 2026 earnings — certification progress update and confirmation of adjusted EBITDA loss guidance ($170M-$200M)
Initial US air-taxi operations under the FAA eVTOL Integration Pilot Program
FAA type certification milestones for the Midnight aircraft
UAE/Abu Dhabi air-taxi program launch progress
Anduril defense partnership — hybrid aircraft development and defense contract awards
LA28 Olympics official air-taxi provider service window

key_risks: Pre-revenue with FY2025 net loss of ($618.2M) and adjusted EBITDA loss of ($481.8M); multi-year path to profitability
FAA type certification is the binary gating event; delays would push commercialization and revenue materially further out
Quarterly adjusted EBITDA losses of $170M-$200M mean continued cash burn and likely future dilution despite ~$1.8B liquidity
Intense competition, especially from Joby Aviation, in a nascent and unproven air-mobility market
Execution risk in scaling manufacturing and standing up US and UAE pilot programs simultaneously
Sector sentiment and macro risk: eVTOL valuations are volatile and sensitive to funding conditions and regulatory tone
